questions.question: What are the top two or three quantified performance targets?
questions.why: The scratch architecture needs numeric anchors to avoid becoming assumption-heavy.
questions.expectedAnswerFormat: Metric name, value and unit for each target.
questions.exampleAnswer: Target output, capacity or throughput; runtime or duty cycle; size, mass or cost constraint.

questions.question: What operating envelope should the design satisfy?
questions.why: Envelope requirements drive module sizing, interfaces, safety protection and later BoM scope.
questions.expectedAnswerFormat: A short list of dimensions, duty cycle, environment, runtime, capacity or output constraints.
questions.exampleAnswer: Dimensions, deployment environment, runtime/duty cycle, electrical/fluid/data boundaries.

questions.question: What external systems, users or infrastructure must this design interface with?
questions.why: External interfaces shape module boundaries and prevent missing integration modules.
questions.expectedAnswerFormat: List each external interface and any protocol, voltage, fluid, data or mechanical constraint.
questions.exampleAnswer: Power, data, mechanical, thermal, fluid, user and service interfaces.

questions.question: Are there named standards, hazards or certification targets that must be treated as in-scope?
questions.why: Regulatory and hazard assumptions should be explicit before reviewer evidence or sourcing work starts.
questions.expectedAnswerFormat: Named standard, jurisdiction, hazard or certification target.
questions.exampleAnswer: Relevant standards, jurisdiction, safety hazards and certification target.
